mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 8.0%, it signals a weak labor market and economic slowdown, causing investors to reduce equity exposure and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE > 8.0%, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates broad-based consumer demand weakness, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as earnings expectations decline.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% from prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline > 0.5%, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle expansion, rising industrial production (INDPRO) signals strengthening manufacturing output and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate profits rise.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when the regime is early-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 0.5%, it signals monetary tightening that increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.5%, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) reflects strong consumer demand for housing and broader economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations rise.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST is rising, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates labor market deterioration, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as economic contraction fears increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decline > 0.5% and UNRATE rise > 0.2% from prior month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS declines > 0.5% and UNRATE rises > 0.2%, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate profit expectations rise.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO is rising, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.05.
